title: Common Phrasal Verbs list 1
intro: Learn the most common phrasal verbs in English with the following list.

meanings: To obey or to follow a rule.
items.example: Everyone has to abide by the rules.

meanings: To require or request someone or something.
items.example: This situation calls for a quick decision.

meanings: To cancel an event.
items.example: They called off the match because of the rain.

meanings: To phone someone.
items.example: I'll call you up when I get home.

meanings: To become less anxious.
items.example: Calm down and tell me what happened.

meanings: When you get overwhelmed by a situation.
items.example: Don't get carried away by the excitement.

meanings: To continue doing something; an activity, a performance, etc.
To behave in a way that is not appropriate.
items.example: Carry on with your work, please.

meanings: To execute a plan.
items.example: The scientists carried out an experiment.

meanings: To extend something from one time to another.
items.example: You can carry over five days of holiday to next year.

meanings: To start doing something you like with enthusiasm.
items.example: She dived into her new project with energy.

meanings: To make someone get interested in something.
To approach someone or something.
items.example: The beautiful pictures drew me in.

meanings: To make something prolong how long it lasts.
To obtain or elicit something.
items.example: The meeting was drawn out for three hours.

meanings: To write or plan something.
items.example: The lawyer drew up a new contract.

meanings: To wear formal clothes for a special event.
items.example: We dressed up for the wedding.

items.es: acabar, terminar (en un lugar o situación)
meanings: To find yourself in a particular situation or place.
items.example: We got lost and ended up at the beach.

meanings: When something breaks into pieces.
When you experience a breakdown in a relationship or something planned
items.example: My old shoes are falling apart.

meanings: When you disagree with someone else.
When something becomes detached.
items.example: Tom and his brother fell out over money.

meanings: When you understand something through reasoning.
items.example: I can't figure out how this machine works.

items.es: reemplazar, cubrir a alguien (en el trabajo)
meanings: When you take someone’s place in their job temporarily because of their absence.
items.example: Can you fill in for me tomorrow?

meanings: To provide information in a document.
items.example: Please fill in this form.
